summary: Go ExitWorktree has the visible keep/remove action names and basic git worktree removal flow, but it is not fully aligned with the TS reference. The biggest divergences are structured output, current-session scoping, fail-closed change detection, restoration of session/tool state, hook-based worktree lifecycle, tmux lifecycle, destructive-permission metadata, cleanup failure semantics, strict input validation, and real-git regression coverage. Several Go helpers exist toward parity, such as persisted WorktreeState, cache invalidator hooks, ResponseJSON, and discovery metadata, but ExitWorktree does not yet wire them into the same runtime contract as TS.

gaps.title: Go returns free-form text instead of the TS structured output object
gaps.description: TS declares an output schema and returns { data: ... } containing action, originalCwd, worktreePath, worktreeBranch, tmuxSessionName, discardedFiles, discardedCommits, and message. The UI renderer consumes those fields. Go ExitWorktree returns plain ToolResult.Content strings such as 'Worktree session ended (kept)' or 'Worktree removed and branch deleted', with no JSON object or stable typed fields. Go has a ResponseJSON helper elsewhere, but ExitWorktree does not use it.

ts_evidence.note: TS outputSchema defines the structured output fields.
The keep path returns data.action, originalCwd, worktreePath, worktreeBranch, tmuxSessionName, and message.
The remove path returns data.action, originalCwd, worktreePath, worktreeBranch, discardedFiles, discardedCommits, and message.
The TS renderer reads output.action, output.worktreeBranch, and output.originalCwd.

go_evidence.note: Go ToolResult exposes string Content plus optional metadata/content blocks, not a typed ExitWorktree data object.
The keep path returns formatted plain text and status/session markers.
The branch-failure and success remove paths return formatted plain text.
A JSON response helper exists, so the gap is ExitWorktree wiring rather than a missing framework primitive.

gaps.impact: Downstream consumers cannot rely on the TS field names, discarded counts, tmux data, or renderer contract; tests are forced to scrape prose.

gaps.title: Current-session scope guard is broader in Go because ExitWorktree reloads repo-wide persisted state
gaps.description: TS gates ExitWorktree on getCurrentWorktreeSession(), with an explicit message that manually created worktrees and worktrees from a previous session are not touched unless the session has been restored into currentWorktreeSession. Go, when inactive in memory, calls canonicalGitRoot and loadFromDisk before deciding no session exists. That repo-wide .claude/worktree-session.json path lets a later process/session exit state created elsewhere, which is a broader lifecycle surface than the TS current-session guard.

ts_evidence.note: TS validateInput rejects when getCurrentWorktreeSession() is null and says it only operates on EnterWorktree in the current session.
currentWorktreeSession is in-memory module state; restoreWorktreeSession is the explicit way to repopulate it.
Resume repopulates currentWorktreeSession from transcript state only after chdir succeeds and clears stale state when the directory is gone.
TS worktree persistence is session transcript metadata keyed by sessionId, not a repo-wide active-state file.

go_evidence.note: Go reads .claude/worktree-session.json for a repo and copies persisted active state into the tool state.
EnterWorktree writes StateFile into repo-local persisted state.
ExitWorktree loads from disk when t.State.Active is false before deciding no session is active.
SetupRegistry creates one shared WorktreeState for EnterWorktree and ExitWorktree, with no injected sessionId scope.

gaps.impact: Go can act on stale or cross-session worktree state that TS would treat as out of scope, and stale state-file recovery may remove or keep the wrong session lifecycle record.

gaps.title: No-active-session and invalid-input semantics differ from TS validation
gaps.description: TS uses validateInput to reject no-active-session with result:false and errorCode 1 before call() runs, and zod enum validation rejects invalid action at schema validation time. Go checks for an active session before validating action and returns a non-error success ToolResult '(no worktree session active)' when inactive. As a result, an invalid action with no active state is reported as no-op success in Go, while TS would reject the action or active-session validation through the tool validation path.

ts_evidence.note: TS strict schema constrains action to 'keep' or 'remove'.
TS validateInput returns result:false, message, and errorCode:1 when no active session exists.
call() also defensively throws if the mutable session disappeared after validation.

go_evidence.note: Go parses input, reloads disk state, and returns ToolResult{Content:'(no worktree session active)'} without IsError when inactive.
Go validates action only after the active-session check.
The existing Go test asserts no-active-session is not an error and exact content is '(no worktree session active)'.

gaps.impact: Model-visible error handling, retry behavior, and validation ordering differ from TS; Go can silently accept bad inputs when no worktree state is active.

gaps.title: Remove safety does not use TS originalHeadCommit baseline and does not fail closed on unknown state
gaps.description: TS countWorktreeChanges fails closed when git status fails, originalHeadCommit is missing, or rev-list fails; it counts commits with originalHeadCommit..HEAD. Go WorktreeState does not record originalHeadCommit. The remove guard ignores the git status error, only checks non-empty combined output, and unmergedCommits compares against origin/<branch> or origin/HEAD. If no candidate upstream can be verified, Go returns ok=false and proceeds as if there were no commits. This is materially different from TS, which treats unknown state as unsafe unless discard_changes is true.

ts_evidence.note: countWorktreeChanges returns null on status failure, missing originalHeadCommit, or rev-list failure, and counts originalHeadCommit..HEAD.
remove without discard_changes rejects unknown state with errorCode 3 and rejects changed files or commits with errorCode 2.
createWorktreeForSession records originalHeadCommit in the active WorktreeSession.
The prompt says remove refuses uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch unless discard_changes is true.

go_evidence.note: WorktreeState has Active, Path, Branch, OriginalDir, RepoRoot, StateFile, and CreatedHere, but no original head commit baseline.
Go ignores the git status error and only blocks when statusOut is non-empty.
Go checks commits only through unmergedCommits and only blocks when ok is true and output is non-empty.
unmergedCommits tries origin/<branch> and origin/HEAD; if neither works it returns '', false and callers proceed.

gaps.impact: Go may remove a worktree without discard_changes even when commits exist relative to the creation baseline or when git state cannot be verified. It also cannot produce TS discardedCommits accurately.

gaps.title: ExitWorktree does not restore the broader session/tool runtime state that TS restores
gaps.description: TS restoreSessionToOriginalCwd resets Shell cwd, originalCwd, conditionally projectRoot and hook snapshots, clears persisted worktree state, system prompt sections, memory-file caches, and plans directory cache. Go ExitWorktree only conditionally os.Chdir's the process and calls InvalidateWorktreeCaches, but ExitWorktree owns only WorktreeState and cannot update BashTool.CWD, RuntimeScope, PlanState, BackgroundTasks, TodoStore, CronStore, file allowed dirs, or MCP settings. RegistryDeps.UpdateSessionContext has the needed shape, but it is not wired into ExitWorktree. The cache invalidator registry has no production registrations in the searched code.

ts_evidence.note: TS restoreSessionToOriginalCwd updates cwd/originalCwd/projectRoot/hooks snapshot and clears worktree state, system prompt sections, memory caches, and plans cache.
The keep path calls keepWorktree then restoreSessionToOriginalCwd.
The remove path kills tmux if needed, cleanupWorktree, then restoreSessionToOriginalCwd.
TS resume also clears CWD-derived caches when restoring a worktree session.

go_evidence.note: Go restoreOriginalDir conditionally calls os.Chdir(originalDir) only when the process cwd is inside the worktree path.
The keep path calls restoreOriginalDir, InvalidateWorktreeCaches, and clearState, but does not update registered tool dependencies.
The remove path similarly calls restoreOriginalDir and InvalidateWorktreeCaches before git removal.
Go provides a generic invalidator registry, but it only runs callbacks that have been registered elsewhere.

RegistryDeps.UpdateSessionContext can update RuntimeScope, PlanState, background tasks, Todo/Cron stores, Bash/PowerShell CWD, file allowed dirs, TeamManager, and MCP settings, but ExitWorktree has no reference to it.
Bash commands run with BashTool.CWD when set, so os.Chdir alone does not necessarily update the shell tool's execution root.

gaps.impact: After exiting a worktree, subsequent Go tool calls can still use stale tool-local CWD, scoped stores, allowed dirs, MCP config, or caches, while TS actively restores them.

gaps.title: Hook-based worktree exit/removal is not equivalent
gaps.description: TS supports hook-based worktree sessions: createWorktreeForSession records hookBased state and cleanupWorktree delegates removal to WorktreeRemove. Go declares a hook bridge and EnterWorktree can call WorktreeCreate in non-git directories, but that branch returns immediately without recording an active WorktreeState. WorktreeState has no HookBased field, and ExitWorktree always uses git worktree remove and git branch -D for action='remove'. The default Go bridge is also a no-op in-memory placeholder unless runtime code replaces it.

ts_evidence.note: TS WorktreeSession includes hookBased and tmux/session fields.
TS hook-based creation populates currentWorktreeSession with hookBased:true.
TS cleanupWorktree delegates hook-based removal to executeWorktreeRemoveHook and handles the no-hook case as preserved.

go_evidence.note: Go declares WorktreeHookBridge with Lookup and Run.
The default in-memory Run implementation is a no-op placeholder.
In the non-git hook branch, EnterWorktree runs WorktreeCreate and returns text without setting State.Active, State.Path, or State.CreatedHere.
WorktreeState has no HookBased field or hook cleanup metadata.
ExitWorktree remove always runs git worktree remove and git branch -D.

gaps.impact: Non-git/hook-created isolation cannot be exited or removed through ExitWorktree with TS-equivalent lifecycle behavior.

gaps.title: Tmux session state is not tracked, killed, or reported like TS
gaps.description: TS WorktreeSession can carry tmuxSessionName. ExitWorktree keep leaves the tmux session running and returns a reattach note, while remove kills the tmux session before cleanup. Go only has a best-effort maybeRenameTmuxWindow helper during EnterWorktree; WorktreeState has no tmux session name, ExitWorktree does not kill tmux on remove, and keep output cannot include the TS reattach note.

ts_evidence.note: TS WorktreeSession includes tmuxSessionName.
TS killTmuxSession wraps tmux kill-session.
ExitWorktree captures tmuxSessionName before cleanup clears the session.
The keep result includes a reattach note when tmuxSessionName exists.
The remove path kills the tmux session before cleanupWorktree.

go_evidence.note: WorktreeState does not store tmux session information.
EnterWorktree only appends maybeRenameTmuxWindow output to creation content.
maybeRenameTmuxWindow renames the current window but does not create or track a tmux session.
ExitWorktree keep/remove paths have no tmux kill or reattach-note handling.

gaps.impact: A TS worktree session with tmux behaves differently on both keep and remove; Go can leave sessions alive and cannot expose tmuxSessionName in output.

gaps.title: Input-level destructive classification for remove is missing in Go
gaps.description: TS marks ExitWorktree as shouldDefer, classifies action='remove' as destructive, and passes the action to the auto-classifier. Go has discovery metadata marking ExitWorktree deferred, but the generic Tool interface has no isDestructive/toAutoClassifierInput equivalent and ExitWorktree does not expose input-sensitive destructive metadata to the permission layer. The remove path can delete a worktree and branch after discard_changes=true without a TS-equivalent classifier surface.

ts_evidence.note: TS sets shouldDefer:true, isDestructive(input) for action='remove', and toAutoClassifierInput(input) = input.action.
The destructive path can kill tmux, cleanup worktree, delete branch, and report discarded commits/files.

go_evidence.note: Go discovery metadata marks ExitWorktree ShouldDefer with a search hint.
The Go Tool interface exposes Name, Description, Schema, and Execute only; no input-level destructive classifier is available.
The Go remove path deletes the worktree and branch through git commands.

gaps.impact: Permission prompts, auto-allow decisions, and audit metadata cannot distinguish keep from destructive remove the same way TS can.

gaps.title: Partial cleanup and failure semantics differ from TS
gaps.description: TS cleanupWorktree catches and logs git remove/branch-delete failures, clears currentWorktreeSession and activeWorktreeSession, and ExitWorktree still returns a structured success message after cleanupWorktree returns. Go returns IsError and leaves state uncleared if git worktree remove fails, while branch deletion failure is returned as a special plain-text success and state is cleared. Go also deletes the branch immediately, while TS waits briefly for git locks before branch deletion.

ts_evidence.note: TS cleanupWorktree logs git remove failures, then clears currentWorktreeSession and activeWorktreeSession.
TS waits 100ms before branch deletion, logs branch deletion failure, and does not throw.
ExitWorktree remove awaits cleanupWorktree, restores session state, logs analytics, and returns a structured remove message.

go_evidence.note: Go returns IsError immediately when git worktree remove fails and does not clear state in that branch.
Go immediately runs git branch -D, clears state on branch delete failure, and returns a plain-text partial-success message.
Existing tests expect remove failure paths to remain IsError/non-success rather than TS-like cleanup logging.

gaps.impact: Retry behavior and session state after partial failures differ. Some Go behavior may be safer, but it is not exact TS parity and should be made deliberate with tests.

gaps.title: Strict object validation and discard_changes schema text are not equivalent
gaps.description: TS uses z.strictObject and describes discard_changes as required when remove would discard uncommitted files or unmerged commits. Go's JSONSchema has the same top-level property names, but no additionalProperties:false representation, parseInputOrError uses json.Unmarshal which ignores unknown fields, and the discard_changes description mentions only uncommitted changes. Go also performs manual action validation after inactive-state handling.

ts_evidence.note: TS inputSchema is z.strictObject with action enum and discard_changes description mentioning uncommitted files or unmerged commits.

go_evidence.note: Go schema declares action and discard_changes but has no strict additional-properties flag and says only uncommitted changes.
parseInput round-trips through json.Unmarshal, which ignores unknown object fields by default.
Go validates action manually after loading/checking active state.

gaps.impact: Unexpected inputs and model guidance differ from TS, especially around committed-but-unmerged work.

gaps.title: Worktree keep/remove analytics with changed-file and commit counts are missing
gaps.description: TS emits tengu_worktree_kept and tengu_worktree_removed with mid_session, commits, and changed_files after recounting at execution time. Go ExitWorktree does not emit an equivalent analytics event or metadata, and because it lacks originalHeadCommit-based counting it cannot currently match the TS counts.

ts_evidence.note: TS recounts changes at execution time and logs tengu_worktree_kept with commits and changed_files.
TS logs tengu_worktree_removed with commits and changed_files.

go_evidence.note: Go keep/remove paths return content but do not emit worktree analytics or metadata.
Go safety checks do not compute a TS-equivalent changedFiles/commits pair for later analytics.
Go has pluggable analytics hooks in other tools, so adding a worktree analytics hook is feasible.

gaps.impact: Operational telemetry and audit trails diverge, and Go cannot report the same discard counters in analytics or output.

gaps.title: Go tests do not lock the TS parity contract for real git removal, structured output, state restoration, hooks, or tmux
gaps.description: Existing Go tests cover simple state clearing, no-active success, substring markers, fake non-git paths, and a cache invalidator callback. They do not use a real git fixture to verify originalHeadCommit..HEAD safety, unknown-state fail-closed behavior, structured JSON output, restored tool-local runtime state, hook-based WorktreeRemove, tmux kill/keep notes, or TS cleanup failure semantics. Several tests currently encode Go-specific behavior that conflicts with TS, such as no-active being non-error and remove failures returning IsError.

ts_evidence.note: Structured output fields need direct conformance tests.
Fail-closed change counting and originalHeadCommit baseline need real git tests.
Runtime state restoration and cache clearing need lifecycle tests.
Hook/git cleanup and branch failure semantics need parity tests.

go_evidence.note: The no-active test asserts Go-specific non-error content.
The remove safety test uses /tmp/non-git behavior rather than a real git fixture.
The discard test explicitly says it cannot easily run real git and verifies failure behavior instead.
Alignment tests check prose markers like session_id= rather than the TS structured output object.
Cache invalidator coverage only verifies manual callback invocation, not production registrations or TS-specific caches.

gaps.impact: Future changes can appear green while preserving Go-only behavior that still diverges from the TS runtime contract.

candidate_tasks.title: Return TS-shaped structured ExitWorktree results and align no-active/invalid-action outcomes
candidate_tasks.description: Introduce an ExitWorktree response struct mirroring the TS output schema and return it through ResponseJSON or the repo's preferred structured-result helper. Validate action before inactive-state handling, return TS-equivalent tool-error semantics for no active session, and preserve exact fields for keep/remove including discardedFiles/discardedCommits when available.
acceptance: action='keep' returns parseable JSON with action, originalCwd, worktreePath, optional worktreeBranch, optional tmuxSessionName, and message.
action='remove' returns parseable JSON with action, originalCwd, worktreePath, optional worktreeBranch, discardedFiles, discardedCommits, and message.
No active session is reported as a tool error/validation failure equivalent to TS, not as successful '(no worktree session active)' prose.
Invalid action is rejected even when there is no active worktree state.
Existing prose-scraping tests are replaced or supplemented with structured field assertions.

candidate_tasks.title: Constrain ExitWorktree to TS-equivalent current-session worktree state
candidate_tasks.description: Replace or scope the repo-wide loadFromDisk behavior so ExitWorktree only operates on worktree state associated with the current session, matching TS currentWorktreeSession/restoreWorktreeSession semantics. If persisted recovery remains required, make it sessionId-keyed and only restore through an explicit resume path.
acceptance: A fresh process in the same repo cannot ExitWorktree a prior session merely because .claude/worktree-session.json exists.
An explicitly restored/resumed session can ExitWorktree after the worktree path still exists.
Stale persisted state whose path no longer exists is cleared without acting on filesystem paths.
Concurrent or separate session IDs do not share a single active WorktreeState unless intentionally restored.

candidate_tasks.title: Implement fail-closed TS change counting with originalHeadCommit baseline
candidate_tasks.description: Add OriginalHeadCommit to WorktreeState/persistedWorktreeState, populate it when entering/creating a git worktree, and implement countWorktreeChanges(path, originalHeadCommit) with TS semantics: git status failure, missing baseline, or rev-list failure returns unknown and remove without discard_changes refuses. Use the same counts for output and analytics.
acceptance: A clean worktree with originalHeadCommit and no changes can be removed without discard_changes.
Uncommitted files block remove without discard_changes and report the file count.
Commits on originalHeadCommit..HEAD block remove without discard_changes even when origin/HEAD would not reveal them.
Missing originalHeadCommit or failing git status/rev-list blocks remove without discard_changes with an unknown-state message.
discard_changes=true proceeds and returns discardedFiles/discardedCommits counts based on the execution-time recount.

candidate_tasks.title: Restore registry/runtime state and concrete caches when exiting a worktree
candidate_tasks.description: Inject a session-context restoration callback or dependency bundle into ExitWorktree so keep/remove can update the same runtime surfaces TS updates: shell CWD, project/runtime scope, plan/background/todo/cron roots, file allowed dirs, MCP settings, and concrete CWD-derived caches. Register real cache invalidators instead of relying on an empty registry. Add a pluggable worktree analytics hook and emit keep/remove events after recounting.
acceptance: After keep/remove, BashTool.CWD and PowerShellTool.CWD point at originalDir when TS would setCwd(originalCwd).
RuntimeScope, PlanState, BackgroundTasks, TodoStore, CronStore, TeamManager, file allowed dirs, and MCP settings are retargeted consistently through the registry restoration path.
System prompt, memory-file, plans, hooks/settings-equivalent caches have production invalidators registered and are invoked on exit.
Worktree keep/remove analytics fire with mid_session=true and changed file/commit counts once TASK-003 is available.
Tests prove tool-local state changes without relying solely on os.Getwd.

candidate_tasks.title: Support hook-based ExitWorktree keep/remove lifecycle
candidate_tasks.description: Track hook-based worktree sessions in WorktreeState, including path/name/session metadata, and make ExitWorktree remove call WorktreeRemove through the configured bridge instead of git. EnterWorktree's hook branch should set active state and persisted session metadata the same way the git branch does.
acceptance: Non-git WorktreeCreate hook success records an active hookBased worktree session.
ExitWorktree action='keep' for hookBased clears/restores session state while preserving the hook-created path.
ExitWorktree action='remove' calls WorktreeRemove with the worktree path and handles no-hook behavior according to TS.
Git worktree removal remains unchanged for non-hook sessions.
Tests use a fake bridge that records WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove calls and payloads.

candidate_tasks.title: Add tmux session tracking and ExitWorktree tmux handling
candidate_tasks.description: Extend WorktreeState/persisted state with TmuxSessionName and provide an injectable tmux killer for tests. Keep should include tmuxSessionName and a reattach note in the structured message; remove should kill the tmux session before cleanup when a session name exists.
acceptance: Keep returns tmuxSessionName in structured output and message includes the TS-style reattach guidance.
Remove invokes tmux kill-session for the stored session name before filesystem cleanup.
No tmux command is attempted when TmuxSessionName is empty.
Tmux failure is handled consistently with TS best-effort behavior.

candidate_tasks.title: Expose input-sensitive destructive metadata for ExitWorktree remove
candidate_tasks.description: Add or reuse a Go tool metadata interface that can classify destructive input and auto-classifier input, then implement it for ExitWorktree so action='remove' is destructive and action='keep' is not. Wire the metadata where the loop/permission layer makes tool approval decisions.
acceptance: ExitWorktree keep is not classified destructive.
ExitWorktree remove is classified destructive before execution.
The classifier input for ExitWorktree is the action string, matching TS toAutoClassifierInput.
Existing deferred discovery metadata remains intact.

candidate_tasks.title: Make cleanup failure and partial-success behavior an explicit TS-parity decision
candidate_tasks.description: Align Go cleanup failure behavior with TS, or document and encode an intentional safer divergence. For exact parity, cleanup should best-effort log/report git remove and branch-delete failures while still clearing active session state and returning the structured remove result. If retaining Go's stricter errors, add an explicit parity-exception note and tests so future audits do not rediscover it.
acceptance: git worktree remove failure behavior is covered by tests and either matches TS clearing/success semantics or is explicitly marked as an intentional divergence.
branch deletion failure behavior is covered by tests and has stable structured output fields.
A short delay or retry strategy around branch deletion is implemented if exact TS lock-release parity is selected.
State clearing after partial cleanup is deterministic and tested.

candidate_tasks.title: Tighten ExitWorktree input schema, descriptions, and conformance tests
candidate_tasks.description: Add strict-object support for schemas or ExitWorktree-specific unknown-field rejection, update discard_changes guidance to mention both uncommitted files and commits, and add focused conformance tests for schema text, unknown inputs, validation ordering, and real git remove guards.
acceptance: Unknown input keys are rejected for ExitWorktree, matching z.strictObject behavior.
discard_changes schema description mentions uncommitted files and unmerged/original-baseline commits.
Validation rejects invalid action before inactive-session handling.
Real git fixture tests cover clean, dirty, committed, unknown-baseline, discard true, structured output, and no-active cases.
